{{Short description|82nd season of the Football League}}

The '''[[1980 in association football|1980]]–[[1981 in association football|81]] season''' was the 82nd completed season of [[English Football League|The Football League]]. This was the final league season with two points for win. 

[[Ron Saunders]] completed the revival of Birmingham club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], as they won the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] for the first time in 71 years. Villa competed in a two-horse race with [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] during the final stages of the season, eventually finishing four points ahead of the Suffolk side. Defending champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] slipped to fifth place, but compensated for this by winning the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] and their first [[EFL Cup|League Cup]]. [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] failed to finish in the top five, a shortcoming that cost Dave Sexton his job as manager; he was succeeded by [[Ron Atkinson]], who had finished fourth in the league and reached the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] quarter-finals with an impressive [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] side – who would suffer a rapid decline after Atkinson's departure.

[[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] endured a dreadful season with just six wins, all at home. They were joined in relegation to the Second Division by [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] and [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].

[[FA Cup]] holders [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] returned to the First Division by becoming [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] champions. Also promoted were [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] and [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], the Welsh club completing a meteoric rise under [[John Toshack]] by going from the Fourth Division to the First in just four years. Both Bristol clubs were relegated, along with [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]].

In the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]], [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] were champions, with [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] and [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] also promoted. [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]], [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] and [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] were relegated, as were [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], who just seven years earlier had finished sixth in the First Division.

The [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] saw [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] finish as champions, with [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]], [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] and [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] occupying the other promotion places. There were no movements between the Fourth Division and the [[National League (English football)|Alliance Premier League]] as the re-election system went in favour of the league's bottom four clubs.

Aston Villa came top of a hotly contested title race to clinch their first top division title since 1910, using only 14 players throughout the season, with only eight scorers. Runners-up Ipswich Town had compensation for their failed title challenge in the shape of a [[UEFA Cup]] triumph, and were also semi-finalists in the FA Cup, their relatively small squad struggling in the final weeks of the season as a challenge for three major trophies took its toll. Arsenal finished third, while West Bromwich Albion enjoyed another strong season and finished fourth. Liverpool finished fifth but won their third [[European Cup]] and their first [[Football League Cup|League Cup]].

Manchester United's failure to finish higher than eighth in the league cost manager [[Dave Sexton]] his job after four trophyless seasons in charge, and a lengthy search for a new manager saw West Bromwich Albion's [[Ron Atkinson]] named as his successor. Everton appointed their former player [[Howard Kendall]] as manager after a disappointing 15th-place finish. Tottenham, meanwhile, only finished 10th in the league but achieved a sixth triumph in the FA Cup at the expense of Manchester City, who climbed up to 12th place in the league after an upturn in fortunes brought about the October change of manager from [[Malcolm Allison]] to [[John Bond (footballer)|John Bond]].

Bond's former club Norwich City went down to the Second Division along with Leicester City and Crystal Palace.

A year after winning the FA Cup, West Ham ended their three-year exile from the First Division by clinching the Second Division title. Notts County, who finished second, went up after 55 years away from the First Division. Third placed Swansea City completed an unprecedented four-season climb from the Fourth Division to the First Division, where they had never previously played. Blackburn Rovers missed out on promotion on goal difference, and then lost their promising young player-manager [[Howard Kendall]] to Everton.

Both [[Bristol]] clubs went down along with Preston North End.

==Election/Re-election to the Football League==
[[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] won the [[Football Conference|Alliance Premier League]] for the second season running and earned the right to apply for election to the [[Football League]] to replace one of the four bottom sides in the 1980–81 [[Football League Fourth Division]]. The vote went as follows:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:left;"
|-
!width=140| Club
!width=185| Final Position
!width=50| Votes
|-
| [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] || 21st (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 48
|-
| [[Hereford United F.C.|Hereford United]] || 22nd (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 46
|-
| [[York City F.C.|York City]] || 24th (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 46
|-
| [[Halifax Town A.F.C.|Halifax Town]] || 23rd (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 41
|-
| [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] || 1st (Alliance Premier League) ||align=center| 15
|}

As a result of this, all four Football League teams were re-elected, and [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] were denied membership of the League.
